Dear AWA People & Culture Team,

I’m writing to join AWA’s Talent Network because your work sits exactly where my experience and my heart meet: helping young people and their families through some of the hardest moments of their lives.

For more than 25 years, I have designed and facilitated learning programs, coached leaders and individuals, and coordinated group programs in person and online, in English and in Spanish. Early in my career in Venezuela, I co-facilitated a community prevention program for adolescents sponsored by Empresas Polar, with workshops on substance use and teen pregnancy prevention for teens living near the company’s facilities. That experience showed me how much prevention depends on reaching families in their own language and reality.

This work is also personal. Addiction to alcohol and drugs has touched my own family, and I have lost a young family member to its consequences. I now have four young grandchildren, and the idea of contributing to prevention efforts that protect children like them means a great deal to me.

I believe I could add value to AWA by supporting staff training and onboarding, developing educational workshops for families, especially Spanish-speaking families, or helping coordinate programs so that teens and parents stay engaged and informed. I’m based in Miami, fully bilingual, and comfortable working remotely or on-site in Miami.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the chance to learn how I could support your team and the families you serve.

Warm regards,
Esther Leon
(713) 504-7640 · leoncesther@gmail.com · linkedin.com/in/esther-leon-ld

I thrive in those exact moments of uncertainty, bringing warmth, clarity, and genuine advocacy to help individuals take that brave first step toward recovery.

In my current role as Lead Program Aide at Beloved Survivors, I manage client intakes, assess support needs, and track service referrals to connect individuals with vital community resources. Whether I am guiding someone through housing options or navigating employment applications, my priority is always making sure no one falls through the cracks. I understand that intake is not just about processing information; it is about building instant trust, listening deeply to a person's barriers and motivations, and walking alongside them with unwavering empathy.

My background spans both compassionate healthcare support and fast-paced operational execution. I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,
Sylvia De La Fuentes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. With over five years of leadership experience in clinical settings, I have successfully supervised multidisciplinary teams and managed programs focused on delivering high-quality care to adolescents and families.

In my current role as Clinical Director at Hope Haven Inc., I oversee a team of approximately 20 staff members, ensuring compliance with CARF standards while fostering a trauma-informed environment. My background includes developing treatment plans, conducting crisis interventions, and maintaining documentation quality, which are crucial for the success of your new facility in North Carolina. I am particularly drawn to your values of kindness, growth, and optimism, which resonate with my leadership philosophy. I am eager to contribute to the launch and ongoing success of your clinic, ensuring that we not only meet but exceed the expectations of the adolescents and families we serve.

Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and vision can support the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am excited to apply for the Creative Group Facilitator position with your PHP and IOP programs. As an art educator, experienced teacher, and graduate student in Clinical Mental Health Counseling with a specialization in Play Therapy, I have built my career around exactly what this role describes: using creative, process-based experiences to help young people express themselves, regulate their emotions, and discover their own capacity to grow.

Over the past couple of years, I have taught process-based art to children and adolescents in a variety of settings. At artNEST Studios, I facilitated weekly after-school art programs for elementary students, designing curriculum that intentionally prioritized creative exploration over the final product. This approach gives participants permission to take risks, make mistakes, and express themselves authentically. I also managed full-cycle logistics for camps, workshops, and parties, adapting programming in real time to different group dynamics, ability levels, and unexpected challenges while maintaining safety standards. These experiences taught me how to read the room, keep a group engaged, and create a warm, inclusive environment where participants feel safe to participate fully.

My work extends beyond the art studio into clinical and crisis contexts. I served as a Volunteer Crisis Counselor with The Trevor Project, providing culturally competent crisis support to LGBTQ+ youth, and I currently volunteer with Harmonia, where my training in crisis de-escalation, harm reduction, and trauma-informed care allows me to provide on-site emotional support to individuals experiencing acute psychological distress.

What draws me most to AWA is the belief that growth happens through connection, creativity, and kindness. I have seen firsthand how a safe space to create can open the door to emotional expression for young people who struggle to put their feelings into words. I would be honored to bring my experience in art facilitation, group management, and trauma-informed support to adolescents in your program, and I can offer consistent weekly or biweekly availability for on-site groups.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my creative practice and clinical training can contribute to your organization.

Warm regards,
Natalia Perez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in joining the clinical team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI) with over 15 years of experience working with adolescents and young adults, I bring a unique combination of clinical training, youth development, experiential education, and a genuine passion for helping young people navigate life's challenges.

My journey into clinical mental health counseling grew naturally from my years working in Jewish education, teen engagement, summer camps, and experiential programming. Throughout these experiences, I discovered that some of the most meaningful growth opportunities happen when young people feel connected, supported, and empowered to explore who they are. This philosophy continues to shape my work as a therapist today.

I earned my Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Lynn University and currently provide individual therapy at Ellie Mental Health. My clinical experience also includes working with adolescents at Family First and with young adults at New Directions for Young Adults, where I facilitated therapeutic groups focused on emotional regulation, interpersonal effectiveness, coping skills, and personal growth. These experiences strengthened my ability to engage clients with diverse clinical needs while balancing therapeutic connection, structured interventions, and individualized treatment goals.

My clinical approach is grounded in Adlerian theory, with an emphasis on belonging, social connection, encouragement, and understanding the patterns that shape how individuals see themselves and the world. I integrate Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), Motivational Interviewing, and experiential interventions to create meaningful growth opportunities. I particularly enjoy incorporating creativity, active engagement, and play into the therapeutic process, recognizing that traditional talk therapy is not always the most effective way to connect with every adolescent.

What draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is your commitment to seeing beyond a teenager's presenting behaviors and recognizing the individual underneath. I strongly believe that adolescents deserve therapeutic spaces where they feel heard, respected, and valued, especially during some of their most challenging moments. Your collaborative, multidisciplinary treatment environment aligns with both my clinical philosophy and my longstanding commitment to supporting young people.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical skills, extensive experience in youth engagement, and enthusiasm for experiential therapeutic work to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and approach could contribute to the meaningful work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

In Community,

Ross Glinkenhouse, MS, Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

Dear Hiring Team,

I’m excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I would be proud to serve as a compassionate and reassuring first point of contact while helping individuals access the treatment and support they need.

I’d love the opportunity to discuss how my background, remote work experience, and skills could be a valuable addition to your admissions team. Thank you for considering my application.

Best,
Blair Dawson

This work taught me to listen carefully, explain next steps clearly, and stay patient when parents are worried.
My customer service background also prepared me for a phone-based admissions role. At Olive Garden, I handled guest questions, requests, and reservations in person and by phone, and I trained new employees on service policies. While working at Kohl's, I supported the store's sales and customer conversion goals. That experience taught me to work toward clear targets while keeping the focus on the person I am helping.
My graduate studies also connect to this work. I am pursuing a Master's in Public Health at Grand Canyon University, where I study the social and behavioral factors that shape health, including mental health and substance use. Although I am new to behavioral health admissions, I learn new systems quickly and am ready to master your intake process, documentation standards, and CRM. Adolescent Wellness Academy's focus on teens and their families matches the work I care about most. Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the chance to discuss how I can support the families who call your team.
Sincerely,
Sara Brown

candidates.cover_letter:
Aray Schuman
Macon, Missouri

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With several years of experience working in human services, crisis intervention, and youth and family support, I believe I bring a strong combination of compassion, communication skills, and organizational experience that would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my current role with Safe Passage Violence Prevention Center, I work closely with children, adolescents, and families who are navigating difficult and often traumatic circumstances. My responsibilities include crisis intervention, case management, safety planning, coordinating referrals, communicating with community partners, and maintaining confidential documentation. This work has taught me the importance of meeting people where they are, listening without judgment, and helping individuals and families navigate overwhelming situations with compassion and understanding.

One of the things I value most about my work is being able to help people during some of their most difficult moments. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming step for both adolescents and their families. I believe the first interaction can make a lasting impression, and I would take pride in helping families feel heard, supported, and comfortable as they navigate the admissions process.

In addition to my direct service experience, I bring strong administrative and communication skills, experience handling sensitive information, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple responsibilities. I am comfortable working with diverse populations, collaborating with professionals across different service areas, and adapting to situations that require patience, professionalism, and sound judgment.

I am interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to continue making a difference in the lives of adolescents and families while growing professionally in the behavioral health field. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, work ethic, and genuine passion for helping others to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and skills could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Aray Schuman

Dear Hiring Team,

When someone finally makes the decision to call for mental health or substance use treatment, how they are treated during that first conversation matters. They may be scared, overwhelmed, frustrated, or simply unsure of what to do next. That is why I am especially interested in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. My experience in behavioral health admissions and intake has taught me how to meet people where they are while still guiding a conversation toward a productive next step. I am comfortable speaking with prospective clients and families, collecting sensitive information, answering questions, coordinating the admissions process, completing documentation, and following up consistently. I also bring the self-direction needed for remote admissions work. I am comfortable managing my own workload and pipeline, keeping track of multiple conversations and next steps, and working within CRM and EMR systems to maintain accurate, confidential records. I believe strong admissions work comes down to both compassion and consistency. People deserve to feel cared for during the conversation, and they also deserve to know that someone will actually follow through afterward. The opportunity to support two programs serving different populations is especially meaningful to me. Whether the person reaching out is a parent trying to find help for their teenager or an adult considering treatment for substance use and mental health concerns, I would approach that conversation with patience, professionalism, and respect. I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my admissions experience, communication skills, reliability, and commitment to helping people access care to your team. Thank you for considering my application and I look forward to speaking with you.

Sincerely,
Savannah Szwarc

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I’m applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. I’ve spent more than 20 years in education, mostly working with middle and high school students in special education. I also have three years of experience as a mental health professional, including two and a half years with Pelican Bay Agency. What drew me to this position is the chance to help teens and their families when they know they need support but aren’t sure where to start.

At Pelican Bay Agency, I worked with children, adults, and families when one or more family members were going through a crisis. I provided crisis intervention, listened to what was happening, and helped them work through the situation and figure out what to do next. That experience taught me how important it is to stay calm, listen first, and explain things in a way people can understand when they already have a lot on their minds.

I took that same approach in education. I remember helping a student who wanted to go to cosmetology school but was overwhelmed by the application and financial aid paperwork. We broke it down together, called the school, and connected with an advisor who helped her get enrolled. I enjoyed that part of my job because I could help someone take a step they weren’t sure how to take on their own.

That’s what I’d bring to your admissions team. When a parent calls about mental health or substance use treatment for their teen, I’d give them room to talk, explain what comes next, and follow up when I say I will. I know that first call can be hard to make, and I’d want families to feel comfortable asking questions.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d appreciate the chance to talk with you about how my experience could help your team and the families you serve.

Sincerely,
Anthony DeVoil

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the caregiving opportunity with Anchor Health Home Care Services.

I bring more than 20 years of experience in the helping field, working with individuals from diverse backgrounds and with a variety of needs. Throughout my career, I have found that providing care goes beyond simply meeting someone's physical needs. It requires patience, compassion, understanding, reliability, and the ability to recognize each person's individual circumstances.

My experience has taught me the importance of treating people with dignity and respect, listening to their concerns, and making sure they feel valued and supported. I take pride in being someone others can depend on, and I believe everyone deserves to feel safe, comfortable, and cared for in their own home.

Helping others has never been just a job to me. It is something I genuinely believe in, and it is what has given my work meaning throughout my career.

I would welcome the opportunity to learn more about your program and how I might contribute to providing quality care and support to Michigan families.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,

Jon Wright

Carol Guess

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to express my strong interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a trained Registered Behavioral Technician (RBT) with hands-on experience supporting youth through structured interventions, skill-building, and crisis de-escalation, I am deeply drawn to your mission of providing compassionate, comprehensive mental health and wellness care for teens.
In my work as an RBT, I have developed a calm, observant, and client-centered approach to behavioral support. My daily responsibilities have centered on implementing individualized treatment plans, facilitating positive peer interactions, and supporting emotional regulation during group transitions and challenging moments. Key strengths I bring to Adolescent Wellness Academy include:
• Behavioral & Emotional Support: Utilizing positive reinforcement, redirection, and structured routines to help young clients navigate frustration, build coping skills, and stay engaged in therapeutic activities.
• Collaborative Care: Partnering closely with Board Certified Behavior Analysts (BCBAs) and multidisciplinary teams to probe new skills, adjust protocols, and maintain safe, supportive environments.
• Objective Documentation: Maintaining accurate, detailed, and insurance-compliant session records that clearly track client progress, demeanor, and behavioral patterns.
I admire Adolescent Wellness Academy’s commitment to helping adolescents heal, connect, and grow together. My background in behavioral health equips me to step seamlessly into a fast-paced clinical or residential setting, build genuine rapport with teens, and uphold the highest standards of patient safety and care.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my RBT training and passion for youth development can support your clinical team and the adolescents you serve.
Sincerely,
Sarah Hall

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator, Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. For more than two years, I have been the person families reach on the hardest day of their lives. I am a crisis receiving clinician at Charlotte Behavioral Health Care. I would like to bring that experience to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

I handle the full admissions process, from first contact to completed admission. I screen adults and children for mental health and substance use needs and decide whether they meet admission criteria. I gather collateral from families, providers, and law enforcement. I am comfortable working remotely and independently. I serve as a remote on-call clinician twice weekly from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m., handling admissions without direct supervision. Before that, I worked full-time as a remote medical scribe for University of Wisconsin Medical. I have extensive EMR experience with Meditech, Epic, MyChart, and SmartCare, and I learn new systems quickly. I speak intermediate Spanish.

Frightened callers need calm, plain language. My training in de-escalation and tactical communication helps me provide it. So does my background teaching about 500 college students, which taught me to explain complex information patiently. I would welcome the chance to bring this experience to your adolescent and adult programs.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how I can support your admissions team.

Sincerely, 

Michael P. Berte

Cover Letter
Amanda Marshel
618-472-4725
amandamarshel320@gmail.com
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with your adolescent mental health and substance use treatment program.
Throughout my professional experience, I have developed strong communication, organization, leadership, and interpersonal skills. My background includes working as a paraprofessional at Wayne City Grade School, working with Child and Family Connections, and owning and operating Alphabet Kids Childcare Center for four years. These experiences have taught me the importance of patience, compassion, dependability, and building trusting relationships with children and families.
Mental health is something I understand on a personal level. Having faced my own mental health challenges, I recognize how difficult it can be to ask for help and how important it is to have someone who listens, understands, and offers support without judgment. These experiences have given me a genuine passion for helping others, especially adolescents who may be struggling and families searching for answers and support.
I understand that the admissions process can be an emotional and overwhelming experience for families. I would approach every conversation with compassion, patience, professionalism, and respect. I would take pride in helping individuals feel comfortable, heard, and supported as they take an important step toward treatment and recovery.
I am a dependable, hardworking individual who is eager to learn and grow in this field. I believe my professional background, personal understanding of mental health, and passion for helping others would allow me to make a positive contribution to your team.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and passion could benefit your organization and the important work you do.
Sincerely,
Amanda Marshel

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I am very interested in this opportunity because it combines my experience in behavioral health admissions with my education and career goals in social work and mental health.

I am also comfortable working independently and learning new systems and processes. I believe my current admissions experience, behavioral health background, and continued social work education would allow me to make a positive contribution to your team.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to speak with you about how my experience and background could fit this position. I look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,

Dominique Whysall

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. The opportunity to be the person who helps someone take that first step toward receiving support is especially meaningful to me. I believe that when people reach out during a difficult time, being met with patience, compassion, and a calm and reassuring voice can make a real difference.

In my recent role as an Eligibility Specialist with the Department of Family Resources, I worked directly with clients to assist with applications, case maintenance, and interviews related to SNAP, TANF, and Health Coverage. This experience taught me how important it is to listen carefully, communicate clearly, protect sensitive information, and help people navigate processes that can feel confusing or overwhelming.

My previous work in education has also shaped the way I approach supporting others. As a Paraprofessional and Instructional Assistant, I worked closely with students with special needs, including providing one-on-one support and implementing behavior-management strategies. I learned to be patient, observant, adaptable, and compassionate while building trusting relationships with students, families, and staff. I understand that every individual has different needs and that sometimes the most important thing you can do is simply listen and meet someone where they are.

I also bring several years of experience as a small-business owner, where I independently managed client relationships, scheduling, records, customer communication, and day-to-day operations. That experience taught me the importance of follow-through, organization, professionalism, and taking ownership of my responsibilities without needing constant direction.

Although my background has not been specifically in behavioral-health or substance-use admissions, the common thread throughout my career has been helping people, communicating with them respectfully, and making sure their needs are heard and addressed. I am eager to bring those skills to an admissions environment and learn the specific processes and systems needed to help your clients and families successfully move toward care.

I would be honored to have the opportunity to contribute to a team whose work can make such an important difference in the lives of adolescents, adults, and their families. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would welcome the opportunity to speak with you about how my experience, compassion, and dedication to helping others could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,

Miranda Baker

Dear Hiring Team,
I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. Knowing that many families reach out on some of the hardest days of their lives, I am deeply drawn to the opportunity to be the calm, compassionate first voice they hear—helping teens and their loved ones feel safe, heard, and supported as they take their first step toward healing.
At the core of my approach to care is a simple belief: we are all just people trying to figure life out, and every environment—whether in person or over the phone—should feel like a true safe space. My goal is always to make mental health support feel accessible, welcoming, and clear rather than intimidating or overwhelming.

Sincerely,
Jaycey Morgan-Tivis

MCKYLA WALKER

PHONE 907-782-6292 EMAIL mckylawalker@gmail.com

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am excited to apply for an opportunity to support individuals and families in their recovery journeys. I bring a strong
background in customer service, human resources, problem-solving, and day-to-day operations, along with something
equally important: lived experience and a genuine commitment to helping others build meaningful, lasting recovery.
For the past two years, I have been actively involved in the recovery community. My own recovery has changed my life in
ways I never could have imagined, and being able to give back has become one of the most meaningful parts of that
journey. It has shown me the power of connection, encouragement, compassion, and meeting people where they are
without judgment. I have learned that recovery is not simply about finding a way forward—it is also about having support,
tools, and people who believe in you as you work to maintain it.
I am ready to take the next step and help more people find recovery and sustain it. I want to use the skills I have
developed through my own recovery, together with my professional experience, to help individuals recognize their
strengths, connect with resources, navigate challenges, and feel supported as they build a healthier future. I understand
that every person's path is different, and I believe in offering respect, patience, encouragement, and a safe, welcoming
environment.
My professional background includes working in automotive repair facilities, where I supported daily operations, quality
assurance, customer service, and team needs. I also bring experience in human resources and the ability to communicate
with people from many different backgrounds. These roles strengthened my organization, adaptability, decision-making,
and problem-solving skills—qualities I would bring to a recovery-focused position.
My lived experience has strengthened my empathy and my understanding of how important inclusive, judgment-free
support can be. I am committed to helping create an environment where people feel heard, respected, and valued,
regardless of where they are in their journey. I would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute to your organization and
continue turning what I have learned into meaningful support for others.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my professional skills, lived
experience, and dedication to recovery could contribute to your team.
Sincerely,
Mckyla Walker

Sincerely,

Natashia Szumczyk

I am excited to apply for the Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Treatment. With over 10 years of experience in behavioral health, mental health advocacy, crisis intervention, and substance use services, I bring a strong commitment to helping individuals and families navigate some of their most challenging moments and connect with the care they need.

My professional experience, combined with my personal understanding of the behavioral health system, has shaped my passion for making treatment more accessible and creating positive experiences for individuals seeking support. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my knowledge, advocacy skills, and dedication to the team at Adolescent Wellness Treatment.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and passion for behavioral health can contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,

Emma Weiss

Dear Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my enthusiastic interest in joining your team to support children, youth, and families. With a strong academic foundation in child development and human services, combined with extensive personal experience caring for and guiding young people, I bring a practical, empathetic, and dedicated skill set that aligns directly with the demands of child welfare and social work.

Throughout my educational coursework and hands-on experience with children and adolescents across various age groups, I have built a deep understanding of developmental milestones, behavioral dynamics, and trauma-informed support. My background has prepared me to handle the core responsibilities of child-centered advocacy, including:

Crisis De-escalation & Emotional Support: Applying patience, active listening, and calm guidance to help youth navigate emotional distress, behavioral challenges, and difficult life transitions.

Child Safety & Behavioral Observation: Maintaining a safe, structured, and protective environment while staying attentive to subtle changes in a child’s physical, emotional, or social well-being.

Care Coordination & Advocacy: Organizing daily routines, supporting educational and developmental goals, and advocating for the best interests of youth in both individual and group settings.

Cultural Sensitivity & Communication: Interacting respectfully with diverse families and youth, maintaining clear boundaries, and upholding strict standards of confidentiality and professional ethics.

My passion for this field comes from a fundamental belief that every child deserves a safe, supportive foundation to grow and succeed. While my background is built on targeted coursework and intensive personal caregiving rather than standard corporate roles, this path has provided me with real-world resilience, adaptability, and an authentic understanding of the day-to-day needs of youth.

I am eager to bring my work ethic, baseline knowledge, and strong commitment to child advocacy to your organization. Thank you for your time and consideration, and I look forward to the possibility of discussing how my experience fits your team's current needs.

Sincerely,

River B. Marlioni

November 19, 2026
Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy & Principles Recovery Center

Dear Hiring Team,

Your posting says many callers reach out on one of the hardest days of their lives. For four and a half years, I was the person on the other end of that moment. I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role, where I can keep helping people take that first step into care.

At Aware Recovery Care, a yearlong in-home addiction treatment program, I worked fully remote as a Family Education Facilitator. My title wasn’t admissions, but at its core my role was the same: I was the first voice families heard, and my job was to help them say yes to care. Before each first call, I reviewed the client’s background so I could meet the family where they were. Many were scared, skeptical, or exhausted. I built trust, explained the treatment process in plain and caring language, and followed up consistently
until they were enrolled and taking part. When our program wasn’t the right fit, I connected them with resources and a clear next step.

I am also comfortable working on my own. After a 2024 restructuring, I was chosen to help build out Aware’s family department and eventually became its only member, supporting families across all 11 states. I managed my own caseload, outreach, and follow-up without daily direction, and I documented every contact in our EHR accurately and in line with HIPAA. I learn new systems quickly and would be glad to get up to speed on Kipu and your CRM.

My master’s in psychology from Harvard focused on why family involvement matters in addiction treatment. That is why AWA’s work with teens and their families, and PRC’s care for adults with co-occurring conditions, both mean a lot to me. I would bring real compassion and steady follow-through to every caller.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can support
your admissions team.

Sincerely,

Pamela Ardizzone

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With more than 20 years of professional experience in education, admissions, academic advising, recruitment, and customer service, combined with my personal commitment to recovery and helping others, I believe my background aligns well with the mission of your organization.

I earned my Bachelor of Arts in History with a minor in Psychology from Texas A&M University. I spent ten years working in Admissions at Texas A&M University and later served as an Academic Advisor in the Department of Biology at both Texas A&M University and Texas A&M University–Kingsville. Most recently, prior to my current position in insurance customer service, I worked as an Admissions Advisor at Southern Careers Institute.

Throughout my career, I have worked closely with students and families, helping them navigate important decisions, overcome personal barriers, and identify appropriate resources. These experiences have strengthened my ability to build trust, communicate with empathy, manage sensitive information, maintain accurate documentation, and guide individuals through unfamiliar and sometimes overwhelming processes.

Beyond my professional qualifications, I bring a personal understanding of substance use and recovery. Having recently celebrated three years in recovery, I understand the importance of compassion, timely intervention, encouragement, and access to appropriate support. I am actively involved in Celebrate Recovery, Kairos Outside, and Prison Fellowship, where my commitment to serving individuals and families facing difficult circumstances continues to grow.

As both a mother and a former educator, I recognize how overwhelming it can be for families seeking help for their children. I would welcome the opportunity to be a compassionate and knowledgeable first point of contact for families navigating adolescent mental health and substance use treatment.

At this stage in my career, I am seeking an opportunity that allows me to combine my professional expertise with work that has a meaningful impact on the lives of others. I believe Adolescent Wellness Academy offers that opportunity.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, qualifications, and commitment to helping others could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,

Monika M. Caylor

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a bachelor's degree in Psychology and Sociology and experience working in behavioral health, crisis intervention, and adolescent assessment, I have found that supporting individuals and families through difficult situations is work I genuinely care about. I would love the opportunity to bring that experience to your team.

In my current role as a Case Manager with Clarvida, I work with both adults and youth experiencing behavioral health crises. A big part of my role involves listening to clients and their families, understanding their needs, worries, and concerns, coordinating services, and helping them navigate, what can often be, an overwhelming time in their lives. Before this, I worked as an Assessment Center Specialist with AmeriCorps at The Village in Pocatello, Idaho, where I conducted youth and family assessments, completed structured screenings, and helped connect families with the resources and support they needed.

What interests me most about this position is the opportunity to be one of the first people families interact with when seeking help for their child. I understand that reaching out for mental health support can be a difficult and sometimes intimidating experience, and I think having someone who is patient, approachable, and genuinely willing to listen can make a meaningful difference. I would love to be that person for families beginning their journey with Adolescent Wellness Academy.

I also bring experience working with virtual platforms through my previous role as a Zoom Video Monitor at Idaho State University, where I managed online classroom operations and troubleshot technical issues. Combined with my background in documentation, communication, and coordinating care, I feel confident in my ability to adapt to a virtual admissions environment.

Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would be excited to bring my experience, compassion, and enthusiasm for helping others to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I appreciate the opportunity to be considered and hope to speak with you soon!

Sincerely,
Taylor Consigny

Dear Hiring Team,

I’m interested in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. What stood out to me about this role is the chance to help families who know they need support but may be unsure where to start. I enjoy helping people feel heard, explaining next steps clearly, and following through so they know what to expect.

My background includes medical reception, hospital administration, behavioral health support, and customer service. As a unit secretary at Navicent Health Baldwin and in my medical receptionist roles, I answered calls, helped patients with scheduling, worked with electronic medical records, and handled private information with care. I also worked as a general clerk at River Edge Behavioral Health and as a child crisis staff member at Hephzibah Children’s Home. Those experiences taught me to stay calm, listen closely, and communicate with patience when someone is having a difficult day.

In my remote customer service role supporting CVS through Alorica, I learned how to stay organized, document calls accurately, and manage my work independently. I’m currently studying Healthcare Administration at Walden University, and I’d like to bring my experience to a role where I can help teens, adults, and families get connected to care.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to talk with you about how my background could support your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Izermee Clowers

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a professional background in healthcare operations, human resources, and client services, I believe my experience supporting individuals and families, managing sensitive situations, and coordinating services would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your admissions team.

During my time as Regional Director of Operations with Griswold Home Care, I developed a strong understanding of the importance of compassion, responsiveness, and clear communication when working with individuals and families seeking care. I regularly navigated sensitive conversations, addressed concerns, coordinated services, and worked to ensure that individuals felt heard, supported, and informed throughout the process.

In my current position as Human Resources Director, I continue to strengthen these skills through confidential communication, documentation management, problem-solving, and coordinating processes that require accuracy and consistent follow-through. I am highly organized, comfortable managing competing priorities, and capable of working independently while maintaining a high level of professionalism.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to be a supportive first point of contact for individuals and families during what may be an incredibly difficult time. I understand how important it is to approach these conversations without judgment, provide reassurance, and help people navigate the next steps toward receiving the care they need.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, strong communication skills, and genuine commitment to helping others to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background could benefit your team.

Sincerely,
Destiny Bryan

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in Adolescent Mental Health and Substance Use Treatment with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With two and a half years of experience working within substance use disorder (SUD) and mental health treatment, I have developed a strong foundation in behavioral health, patient engagement, the intake processes, and case management. I believe my professional experience, interpersonal strengths, and commitment to helping individuals navigate the recovery process make me a strong candidate for this opportunity.

My experience in the behavioral health field includes working at both Twelve Oaks Recovery Center and Banyan Treatment Center, where I have spent approximately equal amounts of time developing my skills in treatment settings. At Twelve Oaks, I served as a Behavioral Health Technician and gained additional leadership experience as a Lead Technician. At Banyan, I continued working as a Behavioral Health Technician before transitioning into my current role as a Case Management and Clinical Intern at the BSW level. In this capacity, I have personally completed multiple case management intake assessments following patient admission and have written dozens of individual weekly progress notes for patients in the outpatient program. During my time as a BHT and throughout my internship I have had the opportunity to work in almost every section of Kipu, developing my understanding and ability to navigate the program effectively. These experiences have strengthened my understanding of patient needs, clinical documentation, communication, and the importance of establishing trust early in the treatment process.

Prior to entering the social work field, I worked as a Front Desk Attendant and Night Auditor with Marriott. Although this experience was outside of healthcare, it provided me with valuable opportunities to develop my problem-solving abilities, communication skills, and experience gathering and managing information during guest reception and registration. I have found that many of these skills translate directly into behavioral health admissions, where professionalism, patience, attention to detail, and the ability to connect with people are essential.

I consider my greatest strengths to be problem-solving, communication, determination, and compassion. Perhaps most importantly, I genuinely believe that all people are inherently good and deserve to be treated with dignity, understanding, and respect. This belief has shaped my approach to social work and my interactions with individuals navigating substance use and mental health challenges. I recognize that the admissions process can be an overwhelming and vulnerable experience for both adolescents and their families, and I would approach each interaction with empathy, patience, and a commitment to helping them feel heard and supported.

I am currently completing my Bachelor of Social Work degree, with an anticipated completion date of December 12, 2026. I have also completed CPR and SBIRT certifications, as well as CPI training, which has since expired. I am eager to continue expanding my knowledge and professional capabilities while building upon the experience I have gained in the behavioral health field.

I am particularly interested in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy because I see this position as an opportunity to broaden my experience in social work while continuing to serve individuals and families affected by mental health and substance use challenges. My background in treatment settings, familiarity with intake and case management processes including Kipu, and genuine passion for helping others would allow me to bring both practical experience and a compassionate perspective to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, strengths, and commitment to the behavioral health field could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you.

Sincerely,

William Chappell

candidates.cover_letter:
I  am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator within your organization. I have a  diverse background in behavioral healthcare, facility management, student support, and customer service, therefore, I will continue to provide compassionate care, create welcoming environments, and ensure the safety and well-being of others. I am very dependable, approachable, organized, and attentive to the needs of every individual I assist. I believe my combination of hands-on care experience, leadership skills, and commitment to helping others would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my current role as a Mental Health Technician at Lincoln Trail Behavioral Health System, I work directly with patients to ensure safety, support, and comfortability. My responsibilities include conducting regular safety checks, assisting with daily living activities, documenting patient information, monitoring vital signs, and facilitating therapeutic group sessions focused on healthy behaviors and positive coping strategies. I also communicate with nursing staff regarding patient needs. If needed, I use crisis intervention and de-escalation techniques to help maintain a safe and supportive unit. This position has strengthened my patience, empathy, attention to detail, and ability to remain calm in challenging situations. Most importantly, it has taught me the importance of treating every individual with repsect and care.

My experience at UC Davis Student Unions has also equipped me with valuable customer service, administrative, and leadership skills. As a Building Supervisor and Information Desk Attendant, I helped students, faculty, families, and visitors by answering questions, providing directions, managing reservations, maintaining accurate records, and coordinating with campus departments. I also attended medical and building emergencies by following established safety procedures. These responsibilities enhanced my ability to multitask, communicate effectively, resolve conflicts, and create a welcoming first impression. Therefore, I was able to train new employees. I always remember that whether a patient is entering a healthcare facility or a patron is approaching a front desk, the way they are greeted and supported can significantly influence their experience.

Additionally, my experience as a Health and Wellness Mentor, youth instructor, and daycare assistant has deepened my passion for helping people from different backgrounds and stages of life. I have mentored individuals with intellectual disabilities and assisted young children with their daily routines, meals, and developmental activities.These experiences have taught me to adapt my communication style,  encourage independence while also being their support system, and build trusting relationships with patience and understanding.

I would describe myself as compassionate, reliable, detail-oriented, and a strong communicator. I work collaboratively with a team, but can also take lead. I handle sensitive information responsibly and manage multiple priorities while maintaining a positive attitude. Whether I am assisting a patient, welcoming a visitor at the front desk, supporting a family by answering their questions, or helping a team navigate a challenging situation, I strive to make people feel respected and supported.

I would love to bring my strong work ethic and genuine passion for helping others to your organization. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and personal qualities align with your team's needs and how I can positively contribute organization.

candidates.cover_letter:
I’m applying for a position with Adolescent Wellness Academy because I want to continue working with teens in a setting where they feel understood and supported. I earned my B.S. in Psychology from Brigham Young University and bring experience as a registered behavior technician, as an intern at a youth crisis center, and as a psychology researcher.

During my internship at Wasatch Behavioral Health, I worked with therapists to develop a goal-setting activity for adolescents at the youth crisis center. We designed it to help teens connect a health goal to something they personally cared about and identify a step they felt ready to take. I enjoyed finding a way to make goal-setting feel relevant to each teen’s life. As a registered behavior technician, I also learned to provide consistent one-on-one support, adjust my communication to each client, and document progress while following individualized plans under supervision.

My research at BYU has given me another way to think about supporting behavior change. In the Health and Development Psychology Lab, I developed a proposal on how personal values might help people follow through on health goals. In the Personality and Close Relationships Lab, I analyzed open-ended responses for a first-author manuscript, which taught me to pay close attention to how people describe their experiences in their own words. As a lab manager, I coordinated meetings, delegated tasks, and kept track of project deadlines. I would bring that same attention to detail and follow-through to your team.

What draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is your commitment to helping teens feel safe and understood while working alongside families. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to that work through direct support, careful documentation, and collaboration with your clinical team. Thank you for considering my application.

candidates.summary:
I hold a B.S. in Psychology from Brigham Young University and bring experience in direct behavioral support, youth crisis services, psychological research, and teaching. My work with children and adolescents has taught me to follow individualized plans, document progress, adapt my communication, and collaborate with supervising clinicians. My research and teaching experience has strengthened my ability to evaluate evidence, explain complex ideas clearly, and coordinate projects with a team.

* Direct behavioral support. As a registered behavior technician at Kids on the Move and Discovery ABA, I provided one-on-one support, implemented individualized treatment plans under supervision, reinforced skill development, and collected session data to track progress.
* Youth crisis services and goal-setting. During my 120+ hour internship at Wasatch Behavioral Health’s youth crisis center, I collaborated with therapists to develop and implement an activity that helped adolescents identify what mattered to them and connect it to an achievable health goal. As an RBT, I also received training and supervision in using acceptance- and values-based strategies specified in clients’ treatment plans.
* Research and data analysis. In BYU’s Personality and Close Relationships Lab, I coded open-ended responses, developed hypotheses, analyzed data, and interpreted findings for a first-author manuscript on personality and partner perceptions. In the Health and Development Psychology Lab, I synthesized research and developed a proposal examining whether personal values can support follow-through on health behavior goals.
* Project coordination and teamwork. As a lab manager in BYU’s GROWTH Lab, I coordinated meetings and timelines, delegated tasks, and helped move maternal and infant health research projects forward.
* Teaching and communication. As a psychometrics teaching assistant, I guided students through lab assignments and explained measurement and statistical concepts during office hours. I also presented research in poster format, translating methods and findings into language a broader audience could follow.

Dear Hiring Team,

I am Cristina, an administrative professional passionate about providing supportive client experiences, clear communication, and effective process management. I am reaching out to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role at Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With over three years of experience in high-volume inquiry management, onboarding, and record keeping, I have a track record of delivering attentive and reliable service to diverse groups.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to be considered for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. My background in healthcare includes patient support, case management, insurance verification, authorizations, and healthcare coordination. Throughout my career, I have enjoyed helping people navigate what can often be a complicated healthcare system, and I believe my experience would translate well to this role.

In my previous positions with EVERSANA, I worked closely with patients and healthcare providers to navigate benefit investigations, coverage issues, authorizations, appeals, and patient assistance programs. I also gained leadership experience supervising a team responsible for patient access services, managing escalated cases, and ensuring patients received the support they needed. My current role with Conifer Health Solutions has further strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, maintain accuracy, and work independently in a remote healthcare environment.

I also bring a personal perspective that I believe would be valuable in this position. As a parent who has navigated the mental health system while advocating for my own child, I understand that seeking help for a child is not always an easy or straightforward process. There can be difficult decisions, uncertainty, fear, and a lot of questions along the way. I understand how important it is for parents to feel that someone is listening, taking their concerns seriously, and helping them understand the options available to their family. I know that the admissions process may be one of the first interactions a family has when reaching out for help, and I would approach those conversations with patience, compassion, and respect.

I would love the opportunity to bring my professional healthcare experience and personal understanding to your team. I believe I offer a combination of administrative knowledge, problem-solving skills, and genuine empathy that would allow me to make a positive contribution to both the admissions team and the families they serve.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and perspective could contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,

Wendy Dalton

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am drawn to this opportunity because it combines several of my strongest skills—communication, organization, problem-solving, and coordinating people and processes—with the opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of adolescents and their families.

Throughout my professional experience, I have developed a strong ability to communicate effectively, manage competing priorities, stay organized in fast-paced environments, and take ownership of responsibilities. My background includes administrative and logistics support, where I handled phone communications, coordinated schedules, tracked shipments and drivers, maintained paperwork, and helped ensure daily operations ran smoothly. Additionally, my three years of professional delivery experience strengthened my independence, accountability, time management, and ability to adapt quickly when circumstances changed.

I understand that admissions coordination in adolescent mental health and substance use treatment requires more than administrative efficiency. It requires patience, empathy, professionalism, discretion, and the ability to make individuals and families feel heard, respected, and supported during potentially difficult moments. I would approach every interaction with compassion while maintaining the organization, follow-through, and attention to detail necessary to keep the admissions process moving efficiently.

I am also comfortable working independently, managing responsibilities without constant supervision, learning new systems, and taking initiative when something needs to be done. I recognize that in a virtual position, reliability, clear communication, and accountability are especially important. I would bring a proactive mindset, a willingness to learn, and a genuine commitment to becoming a dependable member of your team.

What excites me most about this opportunity is the chance to contribute to an organization whose work has the potential to change the direction of a young person’s life. I would be proud to help create a welcoming, supportive first experience for families seeking care and to play a part in connecting adolescents with the resources and treatment they need.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, work ethic, and commitment to providing excellent support could contribute to the success of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Carissa Odasso

Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy
Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator
Dear Hiring Team,
When a parent reaches out about their teen's mental health or substance use, that first call matters. They are often scared, tired and unsure where to start. I want to be the calm and caring voice that helps them take the next step. That is why I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role at Adolescent Wellness Academy.
I currently work as a Qualified Mental Health Professional (QMHP) with Exceptional Wellness Inc, where all of my work is done through telehealth. I reach out to parents, schedule first sessions and support clients through skills training, case management and crisis intervention. I am also certified in the CANS and ANSA assessments, so I am used to asking careful questions, gathering the right information and understanding what a family truly needs. Working remotely has taught me to manage my own caseload, stay organized and keep clear documentation on time.
Before this role, I worked for almost two years as a Registered Behavior Technician with children at BlueSprig Pediatrics and Twinkle Autism Therapy. Talking with parents was a big part of that work. I learned how to listen first, stay steady when emotions run high and explain next steps in a way families can follow. I also learned how much follow through matters. When I tell a family I will call them back, I do.
I hold a Bachelor's degree in Psychology from the University of Houston Clear Lake, and I am currently earning my Master's in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at Our Lady of the Lake University. My graduate training helps me understand the concerns that bring families to treatment and the importance of getting teens the right level of care. I also grew up crossing the border between Mexico and the United States every day for school, and I speak English and Spanish fluently. This helps me connect with families from many different backgrounds.
I learn new systems quickly, and I would bring the same organization I use with my clients to tracking inquiries, following up with families and supporting enrollments in your CRM. I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can help families at Adolescent Wellness Academy from their very first call. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Aranza Hernandez

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admission Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a background in Psychology and Public Health, current graduate training in Marriage and Family Therapy, and professional experience in behavioral support, residential care, client advocacy, and program coordination, I am excited about the opportunity to support adolescents and families navigating mental health and substance use treatment services.

Throughout my professional experience, I have worked with individuals with diverse behavioral, emotional, developmental, and daily living needs. In these roles, I have provided individualized support, maintained confidential documentation, communicated with families and multidisciplinary teams, prepared reports, and helped coordinate services based on individual needs. These experiences have strengthened my ability to communicate effectively, remain organized, manage sensitive information, and approach challenging conversations with patience, empathy, and professionalism.

My experience as a Resident Assistant and Residential Counselor further developed my ability to build trusting relationships while supporting individuals through challenging situations. I provided mentorship, conflict resolution, crisis intervention, and support with independent living skills while collaborating with supervisors, case managers, healthcare professionals, families, and other support staff. Through these experiences, I developed a strong understanding of the importance of meeting individuals where they are, listening without judgment, and helping individuals and families navigate difficult circumstances.

In my current work supporting students, I assist individuals with developing self-advocacy skills, communicating their needs, navigating interpersonal challenges, and building greater independence. This experience has strengthened my understanding of individualized, person-centered care and the importance of looking beyond behaviors to better understand the needs and circumstances of each individual. I believe this perspective would be particularly valuable when communicating with adolescents and families seeking mental health or substance use treatment, as the admission process can be an important and sometimes overwhelming first step toward receiving support.

I am also a Spanish-speaking professional and am able to communicate with Spanish-speaking individuals and families. I value culturally responsive communication and understand how important it is for families to feel respected, understood, and supported when navigating behavioral health services. I would be committed to creating a welcoming and supportive admission experience while ensuring families receive clear information and guidance throughout the process.

I am particularly interested in this position because it brings together my interests in adolescent mental health, family support, and behavioral health services. My academic background in Psychology and Public Health, combined with my graduate training in Marriage and Family Therapy, has strengthened my commitment to supporting adolescents and families through challenging life experiences. I would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute my background in behavioral support, communication, advocacy, and service coordination to Adolescent Wellness Academy while continuing to grow professionally in the mental health field.

Elizabeth Bacilio

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a professional background in legal intake, client relations, and high-volume customer service, I have developed a strong ability to communicate with individuals during sensitive and often overwhelming circumstances. I believe my experience, interpersonal skills, and genuine approach to helping others would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your admissions team.

In my current role as an Intake Specialist and Legal Assistant with the Law Offices of A. Sam Jubran, I serve as an initial point of contact for individuals seeking legal assistance. My responsibilities include conducting intake interviews, gathering sensitive personal information, assessing initial client needs, maintaining confidential records, and facilitating communication between clients, attorneys, and legal staff. This experience has taught me the importance of approaching every interaction with patience, empathy, professionalism, and an understanding that individuals may be reaching out during some of the most difficult moments in their lives.

I have learned that effective communication extends beyond simply answering questions or collecting information. It requires active listening, recognizing individual concerns, establishing trust, and helping people feel comfortable enough to share their circumstances without feeling judged or dismissed. I understand the importance of remaining compassionate while maintaining professional boundaries, protecting confidential information, and ensuring that individuals are connected with the appropriate resources and professionals.

Additionally, my previous experience as a Customer Service Expert with Select Portfolio Servicing strengthened my ability to manage a high volume of inbound and outbound calls, navigate sensitive financial matters, resolve concerns, and maintain effective communication in a remote work environment. These experiences have prepared me to manage the demands of a virtual admissions setting while remaining organized, attentive, and responsive.

What particularly interests me about Adolescent Wellness Academy is the opportunity to contribute to an organization focused on supporting adolescents and families who may be navigating challenging and life-changing circumstances. I recognize that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an incredibly vulnerable decision for both adolescents and their families. I would approach those conversations with compassion, discretion, patience, and an understanding of the importance of making individuals feel supported throughout the admissions process.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my communication skills, administrative experience, and client-centered approach to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and professional strengths may align with the needs of your team.

Sincerely,
Charisma Brown

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. After reviewing the position, I was immediately drawn to the opportunity because it brings together two areas I am deeply passionate about: mental health care and helping individuals and families navigate some of the most difficult moments in their lives.

I bring eight years of experience working at Children’s Health Dallas, where I have had the opportunity to care for pediatric patients across various clinical settings, including the Emergency Department, intensive care, and inpatient units. A significant part of my experience has involved working directly with children and adolescents experiencing behavioral health emergencies, suicidal ideation, self-harm, and emotional crises. These experiences have taught me that the way we communicate with patients and families during vulnerable moments can make a lasting difference in their willingness to seek and accept help.

I earned my Bachelor of Science in Child Development and Family Studies with a concentration in Child Life and a minor in Psychology. I am now pursuing my Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at Walden University as a full-time graduate student, with an emphasis in Trauma and Crisis Counseling. Continuing my education in this field has only strengthened my commitment to supporting individuals experiencing mental health challenges, particularly children, adolescents, and their families.

Throughout my healthcare career, I have developed strong communication, organizational, and patient coordination skills. I understand the importance of listening without judgment, recognizing when someone may be in crisis, maintaining confidentiality, and communicating clearly with families and healthcare professionals. My experience in both direct patient care and healthcare education has also prepared me to manage competing responsibilities, maintain detailed documentation, and approach sensitive conversations with patience and professionalism.

What stands out to me most about this opportunity is the responsibility of being the first person someone speaks with when reaching out for help. I understand that making that initial call can be incredibly difficult, especially for a parent concerned about their child’s mental health or an individual seeking substance use treatment. I would take that responsibility seriously and strive to ensure every caller feels heard, respected, and supported while being guided toward the appropriate next steps.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my clinical background, knowledge of adolescent behavioral health, and genuine passion for mental health advocacy to your admissions team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and dedication align with the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,
Lauren Turner

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy, 

I am writing to express my interest in joining the Adolescent Wellness Academy team. Having worked in inpatient mental health treatment, substance use treatment, and healthcare customer service, I have a deep understanding of the value of patient-centered, compassionate care. I am especially drawn to AWA's goal of establishing a secure setting where adolescents struggling with mental health and substance use issues feel valued, understood, and supported.

My interest in behaviroal health is both professional and deeply personal. I experienced the loss of my late partner to suicide. He was an Army veteran who struggled with PTSD, mental health challenges, and substance use following his deployment. Witnessing the difficulties he faced in navigating life after military service at such a young age profoundly influenced my understanding of the connection between mental health, addiction, and access to meaningful support. His story is a significant part of why I chose this career path. I hope to contribute to a future where individuals and families feel less alone when navigating these challenges. 

Professionally, I have gained hands-on experience supporting adolescents and adults in inpatient psychiatric settings at Snowden at Fredericksburg, as well as individuals receiving substance use treatment at Warsaw Recovery Center. My responsibilities have allowed me to develop skills in patient observation, therapeutic communication, documentation, and maintaining safe and supportive treatment environments. I also bring experience with electronic health record systems, including Epic and Kipu, along with a background in healthcare technology and customer support through TELUS Health.

My long-term goal is to obtain my clinical licensure and specialize in mental health and addiction therapy. I recognize that this journey requires continued education, professional development, supervision, and a willingness to learn. I am not entering this field with the expectation that I can save anyone. Rather I hope to make a meaningful impact, even if it is through one conversation, one moment of feeling heard, or one reminder that someone does not have to navigate recovery alone. 

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my experience, compassion, and dedication to the Adolescent Wellness Academy team while continuing to grow professionally. Thank you for considering my application. I would be grateful for the opportunity to discuss how my background and commitment to behavioral health align with your organization's mission. 

Sincerely,
Kassidy-Ann White
