I’m writing to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at your adolescent mental health and substance use treatment center. My background as a public school secretary, medical office assistant, and military move coordinator has taught me to handle sensitive information, communicate clearly, and keep track of details when families are navigating stressful situations.

This work is personal to me. As a mother, I’ve supported my own children through substance use challenges. I know how hard it can be for a parent to make that first call when they’re worried about their child and unsure where to turn. That experience is why I want to be someone families can count on to listen without judgment, answer their questions, and help them understand what happens next.

As a school secretary, I communicated with families and staff and handled confidential information with care. In a dermatology office, I supported patients in a healthcare setting. As a military move coordinator, I helped families manage paperwork, deadlines, and multiple points of contact. I would bring that same attention to detail to responding to admissions inquiries, coordinating with your treatment team, and following up with families by phone and email.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to bring both my administrative experience and my perspective as a parent to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Jillina Pagliarulo

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With my hands-on experience working in adolescent residential behavioral health, I have developed a strong understanding of the challenges youth and their families face when navigating mental health treatment. I am passionate about helping individuals access the care they need and would love the opportunity to contribute to your admissions team.

I currently work as a Residential Behavioral Health Worker at Mary Hill Youth & Family Center through Integrated Services for Behavioral Health, where I provide direct support to adolescent girls ages 13–17. In this role, I work closely with youth experiencing a variety of mental health and behavioral challenges. My responsibilities include assisting with crisis de-escalation, providing emotional support, maintaining a safe and structured environment, documenting client behaviors and progress, and communicating with other staff members to ensure consistent care.

One of the most valuable things I have learned from working in residential treatment is how important compassion, patience, and communication are when supporting individuals during difficult moments. I have worked with adolescents who struggle to express their emotions, manage challenging situations, and adjust to receiving treatment. These experiences have taught me how to listen without judgment, build trust, and help individuals feel heard and supported.

I am especially interested in this position because I understand how difficult the decision to seek mental health treatment can be for both adolescents and their families. Having worked directly with youth in a treatment setting, I recognize the importance of making that first interaction a positive and reassuring experience. I would be excited to help families understand their options, answer questions, coordinate next steps, and make the admissions process feel less overwhelming.

In addition to my residential behavioral health experience, my education at Ohio University has strengthened my knowledge of healthcare and patient-centered communication. I am organized, dependable, comfortable handling sensitive information, and able to remain professional in fast-paced and emotionally challenging situations.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my residential treatment experience, compassion, and dedication to behavioral health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience could benefit your team.

Sincerely,
Makalin Stadtler

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to have the opportunity to apply to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Your mission to create a safe, compassionate, and supportive environment for adolescents facing mental health challenges aligns closely with my values, education, and experience. I am passionate about helping others feel seen, heard, and valued, and I welcome the opportunity to contribute to a team making a meaningful difference in young people's lives.

I hold a bachelor's degree in Psychology with a minor in Family Science and am currently pursuing a master's degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling. I have four years of experience as a Registered Behavior Technician, providing one-on-one support to children and adolescents up to age 18 on the autism spectrum in home and clinical settings. In this role, I implemented evidence-based interventions, monitored client progress through data collection, and maintained a safe, supportive environment. As an Intervention Specialist, I also supported elementary-aged students with their academic, behavioral, and individual needs.

Beyond my direct experience working with children, I have developed strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills. In my role leading volunteer operations for my church, I had the privilege of training and supervising more than 30 volunteers a day, ranging in age from 18 to 98. Working with such a diverse group taught me the importance of humility, adaptability, active listening, and recognizing different learning styles. I worked to create an inclusive environment where every individual felt heard and valued while helping improve daily operations through collaboration and individualized training. I also provided administrative support by answering phones, assisting visitors, responding to questions, and coordinating schedules.

I am drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy because of your commitment to connection, compassion, and individualized care. I believe one of the most meaningful things we can offer is a place where individuals feel safe to be themselves and know they are not alone and that they have value and purpose. 

Thank you for considering my application. I would be grateful for the chance to join your team and support the important work you do.

Sincerely, Kaley Rhoton

Carlos Martinez
Miami, FL | (786) 259-5883 | cmartinez1991@hotmail.com

Dear Admissions Hiring Team,

As a Youth Intervention Specialist at Latinos Salud, I helped insured and uninsured clients find preventive healthcare and coordinated referrals to connect them with care.

I’m applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position because I’d like to bring that
experience to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I’m especially drawn to the chance to help a parent seeking support for their teen or an adult
reaching out about treatment understand what happens after that first call.

At Latinos Salud, I learned to listen for the practical question behind a request for help. For someone unsure where to go or how to access services without insurance, a useful conversation meant identifying a service they could reach and explaining how to connect
with it. That experience shapes how I would approach admissions calls. I would listen without judgment, explain the options in everyday language, and make sure the caller
knows who will follow up and when.

In my current remote role at Kantar IBOPE Media, I conduct structured phone interviews, document conversations in Microsoft Power Apps, and coordinate callbacks. When a question requires another team member’s input, I document what needs attention and
ask for guidance. I would bring those same habits to screening calls, scheduling assessments, and keeping referral details accurate for your team.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how
my background in healthcare referrals and remote phone support could serve callers
across both programs.

Sincerely,
Carlos Martinez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

Please accept this application for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) and Principles Recovery Center (PRC). Supporting individuals and families on some of their hardest days requires genuine empathy, calm guidance, and steady follow-through. Bringing 4 years of strong behavioral health administrative experience and a proven remote work background, my goal is to support callers from their very first inquiry through admission.

Over 4 years in behavioral health and substance use administration, my work has centered on supporting clients, families, and referring providers across inpatient and outpatient settings. 

Key qualifications directly align with your team's needs:

• Compassionate first-point-of-contact support: Answering inbound calls and inquiries with a warm, confident phone presence while explaining PHP and IOP levels of care in plain, caring language.
• End-to-end intake coordination: Screening callers for clinical fit, completing insurance verifications, coordinating assessments and intake dates, and managing pre-admission paperwork.
• Consistent, reliable follow-up: Tracking every lead and maintaining steady outreach until each caller is scheduled or connected with appropriate care elsewhere.
• Accurate, HIPAA-compliant documentation: Maintaining detailed records in CRM and EMR systems while quickly adapting to new operational software as needed.

Working remotely as a previous company co-owner strengthened the ability to stay organized, manage high-priority workflows independently, and communicate clearly in a virtual environment. Combined with family-centered communication skills, this background enables meeting callers with patience and clarity when it matters most.
Thank you for your time and consideration and I look forward to the opportunity in discussing how my behavioral health experience can contribute to your growing admissions team across AWA and PRC would be greatly appreciated.


Sincerest Regards, 
Emily Rivera

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Mental Health and Substance Use Treatment. With over five years of healthcare administrative experience and a deep commitment to compassionate patient advocacy, I am eager to bring my skills in insurance verification, electronic health records (EHR) management, and high-volume virtual support to your admissions team.
In my current role as a Patient Representative and Medical Administrative Support specialist at Christus Health, I serve to reassuring first point of contact for patients and families navigating complex healthcare needs. My daily responsibilities include verifying insurance eligibility, coordinating procedure benefits using ICD-10 and CPT coding, managing medical records requests, and scheduling appointments in high-volume clinical settings. Having managed these processes within Epic EHR while strictly upholding HIPAA compliance, I understand how critical speed, empathy, and precision are when families are seeking urgent behavioral health or substance use support.
Prior to CHRISTUS Health, my role as a Customer Service Representative at LINCARE Enteral Services honed my ability to coordinate care remotely across external agencies, verify coverage, and ensure timely documentation for critical patient needs. Additionally, my six years of service as a Correctional Officer with the Texas Department of Criminal Justice (TDCJ) equipped me to remain composed under pressure, de-escalate sensitive situations, and maintain meticulous, compliance-focused records. Together, these experiences allow me to support anxious parents and adolescents with both genuine warmth and operational reliability.
I am highly proficient in virtual communication and administrative tools, including Microsoft Teams, Outlook, Excel, and Workday, making me well-prepared to thrive in a remote admissions environment. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in patient intake, insurance verification, and crisis-ready communication can help families smoothly transition into your care programs.
Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely, 

Haley Ortega

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in adolescent mental health and substance use treatment. With more than 15 years of experience across mortgage services, general management, and the service industry, I bring a strong foundation in communication, organization, relationship-building, and compassionate client support. More importantly, I bring a personal understanding of how deeply mental health and addiction can affect individuals, families, and entire communities.

Throughout my professional career, I have developed the ability to connect with people from all walks of life, listen to their needs, navigate challenging conversations, and help guide them through important decisions. My background in mortgage services has taught me the importance of patience, attention to detail, and helping people navigate complicated and sometimes stressful circumstances. My management and service industry experience have strengthened my ability to multitask, communicate effectively, remain composed under pressure, and make people feel heard and valued.

My interest in this position is also deeply personal. I have navigated my own mental health journey and have had the privilege of knowing many people who have fought through addiction and pursued sobriety. Recently, I experienced the heartbreaking loss of my best friend of 23 years to an overdose. Their struggle with addiction was deeply connected to childhood trauma and abuse. That loss has reinforced my belief that early intervention, compassionate support, and access to the right resources can make a life-changing difference.

I know firsthand that behind every struggle is a person deserving of understanding, dignity, and the opportunity for a better future. I would be honored to play a part in helping adolescents and their families find hope, access meaningful treatment, and recognize that their circumstances today do not have to define their tomorrow. Finding a future worth living for is something I believe everyone deserves the opportunity to experience.

I understand that an Admissions Coordinator is often one of the first points of contact for families navigating some of the most difficult and emotional moments of their lives. I would approach that responsibility with empathy, professionalism, patience, and genuine care. I believe my professional background, interpersonal strengths, and personal perspective would allow me to contribute meaningfully to your team and the families you serve.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to speak with you about how my experience, dedication, and passion for helping others could contribute to the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy. I would be proud to help make a difference in the lives of young people and help families find a path forward when they need it most.

Warm regards,

Reid L Golding

Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am reaching out because I would love the opportunity to join your team. For the past twelve years, my work and life have centered around supporting young people and their families through education, psychology and community work. When I came across this opening at Adolescent Wellness Academy, it immediately caught my attention because it aligns so closely with what I already care about and do every day.
Working in schools and special education for over a decade has taught me how to stay calm, adapt on the fly and truly connect with kids and teens from all walks of life. Alongside my classroom experience, my studies in clinical psychology and applied behavior analysis have helped me better understand what drives behavior and how to support youth through tough moments. Outside of work, I spend a lot of my time organizing local community outreach, mentorship, and family support efforts. I genuinely enjoy meeting new people, hearing their stories, and helping them figure out their next steps.
That same mindset carries over into my customer service background. Whether I am talking to a parent who feels overwhelmed, answering questions for a family, or working alongside a team, I always try to bring warmth, patience, and a steady presence to the room. People tend to feel comfortable opening up to me, and I take pride in making sure they feel heard and supported.
I also want to be completely honest about my administrative background. I have not worked directly in insurance billing before, though I do have plenty of experience writing detailed session notes specifically geared toward insurance billing requirements. I know how much accurate documentation matters behind the scenes. Because I am really excited about this position, I am already taking the initiative to research and learn the basics of behavioral health billing right now so I will not be starting from scratch.
If you bring me onto your team, you will get someone who is trustworthy, dependable, and comfortable working independently without needing to be micromanaged. I show up, do what needs to be done, and step in wherever I am needed. Thank you so much for taking the time to read this, and I look forward to speaking with you all soon.
Sincerely,
Demetria Evans

Dear Hiring Team,

I have been a fearless Women’s Ministry leader at my church since 1999, Faith Assembly of God.  I have participated in motivational speaking opportunities to over 250 women on more than 7 occasions on how to move forward after hitting rock bottom.  I have spoken at conferences and been a Women’s Ministry leader assisting hundreds of women in gaining life skills, coping skills, and accepting responsibility skills.  I have always been interested in counseling as a career.  I have conducted psychotherapy sessions for 10 years at my church with hundreds of elderly and young women.
I took a People Helper Course, 50 hours, back in 1995-1996 and loved it!  I spent a year online counseling people both men and women.  I enjoyed counseling so much that I spent over 100 hours volunteering.  However, I had always wanted to be a teacher, so I went into the field of education.  I was awarded the Sallie Mae Teacher of the Year my first year of teaching.  I’ve been teaching for 27 years, and I want to change careers.  
The program you are using to help students sounds like a perfect fit for me.  Even though my degrees are in education AA, BS, MS, and Ed.S is in Curriculum & Instruction.  I have life experiences writing IEPs and tracking student information with data-driven instruction in curriculum and assessment.  My 27 years as a teacher has afforded me numerous opportunities to work with children who are troubled, dismayed, and signs of lethality.

I can be relied on to maintain confidentiality and follow the rules and procedures.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to combine my professional experience in coordination and customer service with something I genuinely care about: helping individuals and families find the support and resources they need during some of the most difficult periods of their lives.

My interest in this field is also personal. Through my own life experiences, I understand how overwhelming it can be to navigate mental health challenges, search for appropriate treatment, locate community resources, and figure out where to turn when you don’t know what options are available. I know firsthand how much of a difference it can make when someone takes the time to listen, treats you with compassion rather than judgment, and helps you navigate the next steps. I would love the opportunity to be that person for families who may be feeling overwhelmed, scared, or unsure of where to begin.

Professionally, I bring a diverse background in customer service, independent operations, event coordination, and administrative responsibilities. In previous positions, I have been responsible for coordinating activities, communicating with a wide range of individuals, managing schedules and logistics, resolving problems, maintaining organization, and handling multiple responsibilities independently. I have also worked in roles requiring patience, adaptability, strong communication skills, and the ability to remain composed when situations become challenging.

I believe one of my greatest strengths is my ability to understand people without making assumptions about their circumstances. I recognize that every individual and family has a different story, and I would approach every interaction with empathy, patience, professionalism, and respect. I am also comfortable learning new systems, following established procedures, and taking initiative when something needs to be done.

I am looking for a long-term career where I can grow professionally while doing work that has a meaningful impact on other people’s lives. The opportunity to help adolescents and their families take the first steps toward receiving mental health and substance use treatment is something I would take seriously and approach with genuine compassion.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my professional background, personal perspective, and dedication to helping others could make me a valuable addition to the Adolescent Wellness Academy team.

Sincerely,
Amber

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With six years of experience in healthcare, including roles as a Surgery Coordinator and Ophthalmic Scribe, I have developed a strong background in patient communication, care coordination, scheduling, and administrative support. Throughout my time as a Surgery Coordinator, I served as a primary point of contact for patients navigating the surgical process. My responsibilities included coordinating procedures, managing schedules, communicating with patients and medical providers, and ensuring all necessary documentation and preoperative requirements were completed. I understand how overwhelming medical decisions can feel, and I take pride in helping patients feel informed, comfortable, and supported throughout their care.

My experience as an Ophthalmic Scribe has further strengthened my ability to manage detailed medical records, navigate electronic medical record systems, maintain patient confidentiality, and communicate effectively within a fast-paced healthcare environment. These roles have taught me the importance of organization, accuracy, adaptability, and consistent follow-through.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to be a reassuring first point of contact for individuals and families seeking help. While my professional background has primarily been in ophthalmology, I believe the compassion, patience, and communication skills I have developed are directly transferable to admissions coordination. I recognize that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an incredibly vulnerable experience, and I would approach every interaction with empathy, professionalism, and respect.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my healthcare experience, organizational skills, and dedication to patient-centered care to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background could contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,

Victoria Welch

Sincerely,  
Harmony Jones

candidates.cover_letter:
I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment position. With more than a decade of experience in juvenile intake, correctional mental health, crisis intervention, law enforcement, and working with individuals and families during challenging circumstances, I believe I bring a unique combination of professional experience, communication skills, and compassion that would make me a strong addition to your admissions team.

Throughout my career, I have worked with individuals facing difficult personal circumstances, behavioral challenges, mental health concerns, and situations requiring timely intervention and appropriate referrals. As a Juvenile Intake Officer with the Kansas 24th Judicial District, I regularly responded to law enforcement requests involving juvenile offenders and children in need of care. This required assessing circumstances, communicating with families and professionals, coordinating appropriate referrals and placements, and helping determine the next steps for young people during some of their most difficult moments.

My experience as a Corrections Counselor with the Kansas Department of Corrections further strengthened my ability to work with individuals experiencing behavioral and emotional challenges. I helped residents navigate difficult transitions, encouraged positive behavioral changes, supported treatment-related goals, and connected individuals with appropriate resources. I also served as a Due Process Coordinator at Larned State Hospital, where I worked within a mental health treatment environment while maintaining accurate procedures, documentation, and compliance with established policies.

In my current role as a police officer, I continue to rely on strong communication, sound judgment, de-escalation, and the ability to build rapport with people from different backgrounds and circumstances. Outside of law enforcement, my experience as a middle school basketball coach has strengthened my passion for mentoring adolescents, building trust, encouraging positive decisions, and helping young people recognize their potential.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to make a meaningful difference before someone even enters treatment. I understand that the first conversation with a family can be overwhelming, emotional, and sometimes uncertain. I believe those conversations require patience, active listening, compassion, professionalism, and the ability to explain options clearly while helping people move toward a meaningful next step.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my background in juvenile services, behavioral health, crisis intervention, case management, and professional communication to your organization. I am comfortable working with technology, maintaining accurate records, managing competing priorities, and taking responsibility for following through on important tasks. I am also eager to learn your admissions processes, systems, and procedures.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience and commitment to helping adolescents and families could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
John Pritchett
214-735.3707
Illpritch@gmail.com

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. A first call can feel overwhelming for someone seeking treatment or for a family trying to help. In my work in behavioral health, I have learned to listen carefully, explain next steps clearly, and follow through with compassion and discretion.

As a Registered Behavior Technician and Level 3 Trainer at Spectrum of Hope, I communicate with caregivers, BCBAs, and clinical leaders; support client evaluations; and maintain timely, confidential records in CentralReach. I also train new technicians on documentation, professional communication, and client-specific procedures. Balancing direct care, records, and changing priorities has strengthened the organization and judgment I would bring to coordinating assessments and following up with prospective clients.

Working with children and caregivers has shown me how much a calm, respectful interaction matters when a family is navigating care. I would bring that approach to teens and families reaching out to AWA and to adults exploring treatment through PRC. I am also completing a bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration at Western Governors University, and I am eager to help make the path from an initial inquiry to the right care feel clear and manageable.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my behavioral health experience, attention to detail, and commitment to families could support your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Sarah Hawk

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining your organization and contributing my experience, knowledge, and passion for behavioral health and substance use recovery services.

I have worked in residential facilities, community-based programs, treatment settings, and crisis stabilization environments. In addition to my direct service experience, I bring a strong background in leadership, training, and healthcare administration. I believe one of my greatest strengths is my ability to connect with people while maintaining professionalism, accountability, and compassion. I am looking for an opportunity where I can contribute my experience, continue developing professionally, and make a meaningful difference in the lives of the individuals and communities being served. work_history.summary: I am certified to Train individuals to become a Certified Recovery Coach by Facilitating the Recovery Coach Academy which is a 5 day course in order to start working/billing as a Recovery Coach. No billing can be done for Recovery Coaching Services until they have completed the Recovery Coach Academy. As a Certified Trainer/Facilitator I am granted the ability to take part in conducting an RCA training with a fellow Certified Trainer/Facilitator in order to certify a class of individuals to be allowed to work as Recovery Coaches and begin to gain work hours/supervision hours from a Recovery Coach Supervisor in order to complete their Certification. I can Train/Facilitate at any CCAR Sanctioned Recovery Coach Academy class, and currently as I am a Recovery Coach for the Lowell House Addiction Treatment and Recovery, Inc., I am participating as a trainer/facilitator in Recovery Coach Academies set up by the company itself. If I was to participate in training/facilitating an RCA that is not run by LHI, I would have to specifically take time off of work due to LHI not being involved. I have conducted the RCA Training both in person and Virtually over multiple platforms such as ZOOM, and Google Meets.

All Intakes, Insurance Authorizations, Insurance Reauthorizations and Daily Billing is completed by the Recovery Coach as well as any and all eligibility checks. I have login credentials for the Executive Office of Human Services Virtual Gateway page as well as access too REVS for eligibility. I also possess Login Credentials for all MA Health affiliated insurance companies. I have been doing Admission, Billing and Insurance Authorizations/Reauthorizations for 4 years but have been doing it at this company for 2 years.

work_history.title: Senior Recovery Coach/Family Recovery Coach
work_history.company_name: Lowell House Addiction Treatment and Recovery
work_history.summary: Certified CCAR Recovery Coach. Working on a peer to peer platform that is fully Recoveree based. I conduct meetings in office and out in the community. I help everyone from active addicts to those with 20+ years of sobriety, and I help them figure out "what is next". Stopping the use of substances is a monumentally positive achievement and very hard to maintain. That being said, life does not slow down before, during, or after active use. I am here to support and help any and all Recoverees no matter what stage they are at to make their lives manageable. I often get the question, "I stopped doing drugs, that is great, now what?" or "how do i fix all the issues I have created from my substance use?" and this is exactly where I come in as a Recovery Coach. Any and all questions I find answers for. If I cannot answer it myself I will find the appropriate person who can. It is also important to say that I actually do not DO any of the work for a Recoveree. They do all the work themselves, and I just provide guidance and tools. There's no mandatory ANYTHING with Recovery Coaching and that is how we meet the Recoveree where they are at. The recoveree creates a Wellness Plan with me and we track progress towards eat goal no matter what it is or how big or how small the progress might be. All of this while retraining the brain to ditch the "instant Gratification" mind set and molding a positive and personable personal atmosphere. There is no such thing as failure unless you give up and I am here to try anything and everything to get a person where they really want to be and push past their idea of potential and into a whole new realm of what they can do. This also comes with Insurance auth/reauth services, Billing setups, intake/discharge documentation, avid computer skills for written documents, skills in the use of software for maintaining and organizing documentation, digital and paper documentation of all engagements, ESM Virtual Gateway Assessments for BSAS, communicating with other providers within the Recoveree's circle for integrated care, communicating with insurance companies to continue engagement in services, following HIPPA and 42 CFR guidelines and filling out appropriate Release Documentation, and all other forms and documentation required for confidentiality, referrals, and insurance/billing. I also possess logins for the Executive Office of Health and Human Services, and all insurance companies under the MA Health umbrella. I report to a supervisor who previously had my position but is now the Director of a Peer Center owned and operated by LHI and funded by BSAS so I am the only member of my department not in management. I was tasked with writing the entire operational process from start to finish, meeting a client for the first time to discharging after completion, and ALL the processes in-between. This includes the billing, insurance, contact documentation, filing forms for HIPPA and 42 CFR, all the guidelines for BSAS and MA Health Insurance. These book only pertains to the processes of Recovery Coaching specifically at Lowell House Addiction Treatment and Recovery. I will be with Lowell House Addiction Treatment and Recovery for 2 years as of June 2021and hope to be promoted to the Recovery Coach Supervisor for all new interns and New Hires as they will be using the book I created to learn how to do the job. I have conducted all aspects of the job in both in person/office atmospheres as well as at home from a laptop for administrative work and virtually for contacts and meets through multiple platforms such as ZOOM and Goggle Meets.

I come to the role with experience in Admissions in substance use treatment, KIPU, insurance verification, as well as in remote work and managing my own work flow. 

My relevant work experience is at Casa Serena, a treatment center for women struggling with substance use disorder. While in this role I became interested in the intake and admissions process, and had the opportunity to complete intakes for the residential, PHP, and IOP LOC, being the first person that clients interacted with when they came on site. During my time in this role, I was consistently praised for my ability to provide client centered care while balancing administrative needs such as maintaining accurate and timely documentation. Through this work I also learned the importance of maintaining open and clear communication with clients; helping people in their most vulnerable moments by making the processes, timelines, and expectations known in plain and caring language. I believe this is paramount to providing trauma-informed care as it creates solid ground for the clients and returns control. I deeply enjoy holding this space for individuals during their most challenging moments. I would love to translate this experience into working with teens and their families. 
As an Administrative Assistant at Walnut Psychotherapy Center, I have also become familiar with the complexities of insurance benefits and have practiced reading and translating insurance benefits into digestible and usable information. My previous administrative experience speaks also to my ability to track leads, follow up with prospective clients. 

I hope for the opportunity to discuss the role in more detail, and would be excited to join your team as an Admissions Coordinator.

With care,
Kiana Ranjbaran

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager, 

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With a background in mental health services, clinical work, and program support, I bring a combination of administrative, organizational, and interpersonal skills that align well with the responsibilities of this role. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to help individuals and families navigate the process of accessing mental health and substance use treatment during what can often be a difficult and overwhelming time.

In my previous role as a Program Support Specialist within Post-Release Services, I developed experience supporting program operations, coordinating services, maintaining documentation, and communicating with individuals and various service providers. This role strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, maintain organized records, facilitate communication, and ensure that important follow-up tasks were completed. Additionally, my clinical experience has provided me with familiarity with electronic health record systems, timely and accurate documentation, client scheduling, and the importance of maintaining confidentiality and HIPAA-compliant practices.

As a mental health professional, I understand the importance of approaching individuals and families with empathy, patience, and clear communication. I recognize that reaching out for treatment can be a vulnerable first step, particularly for adolescents and their families. I would bring a compassionate, nonjudgmental approach to initial inquiries while maintaining the organization, consistency, and attention to detail necessary to support an effective admissions process. I am also comfortable navigating conversations that require balancing sensitivity with clear communication, follow-through, and appropriate coordination of services.

Although my background has primarily been in clinical and program support settings rather than a dedicated admissions role, I believe these experiences have equipped me with highly transferable skills. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my clinical perspective, administrative capabilities, and commitment to accessible mental health care to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skill set could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Stephanie Lee-Ferreira

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. As a psychology graduate and mental health professional, I am passionate about creating meaningful connections with individuals and families while helping them access the care and support they deserve.

Throughout my professional journey, I have witnessed how overwhelming it can be for families to navigate mental health services, particularly when seeking treatment for their children. My experience working in inpatient psychiatric care at Sheppard Pratt Hospital has reinforced my belief that quality mental health care begins with the very first interaction. Having someone who listens with compassion, communicates clearly, and provides reassurance can make a significant difference in a family's willingness to pursue treatment.

I am particularly drawn to this position because it offers the opportunity to make an impact beyond the clinical setting. I would welcome the responsibility of helping families navigate their next steps, addressing their concerns, and ensuring that the admissions process is both welcoming and efficient. I understand the importance of balancing empathy with professionalism, especially when handling sensitive information and communicating with individuals during vulnerable moments.

I consider myself a dependable, adaptable, and highly motivated individual who takes initiative and approaches challenges with patience and understanding. I am comfortable working independently in a virtual environment while remaining accountable, organized, and connected to a collaborative team.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my leadership experience, passion for youth advocacy, and commitment to behavioral health excellence to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am confident that my skills, professional values, and dedication to serving adolescents and families would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the remote Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over 10 years of experience in healthcare, behavioral health support, and consumer relations, I specialize in guiding individuals and families through sensitive, high-stress decisions with warmth, clarity, and urgency. I deeply admire Adolescent Wellness Academy’s commitment to providing compassionate, specialized mental health and substance use care for teens, and I would be honored to serve as a supportive first point of contact for your families.
Reaching out for adolescent treatment is often one of the most overwhelming moments a parent or guardian will ever face. Serving as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator requires more than administrative precision—it demands active listening, genuine empathy, and the ability to build immediate trust over the phone or screen. Throughout my career, I have developed a strong foundation in these exact areas:
• Empathetic Family & Client Rapport: Experienced in de-escalating crisis moments, listening without judgment, and reassuring anxious parents and caregivers while clearly explaining program options and next steps.
• Seamless Intake & Insurance Navigation: Skilled at conducting thorough initial assessments, verifying insurance benefits accurately, coordinating with clinical teams for level-of-care approvals, and maintaining strict HIPAA compliance in a remote environment.
• Persistent, Organized Follow-Through: Proven ability to manage a high volume of inquiries in CRM and EHR systems, ensuring timely follow-ups so no teen or family falls through the cracks during the critical window between first contact and admission.
Working remotely requires strong self-direction and seamless communication with multidisciplinary teams. My background bridging front-line support and healthcare administration allows me to collaborate effortlessly with clinicians, utilization review specialists, and outreach teams to ensure every transition into care is as smooth and stress-free as possible.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my dedication to behavioral health advocacy, rapport building, and admissions coordination can help Adolescent Wellness Academy connect more teens and families with life-changing care. I can be reached at 812-653-6468 or richardsonfancy@gmail.com to schedule an interview.  

With Gratitude 
Nancy M Richardson

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. As a bilingual English-Spanish professional, virtual Spanish language instructor, and student pursuing an Associate of Applied Science in Human Services with a concentration in Addictions Counseling, I am passionate about supporting individuals and families navigating behavioral health challenges and accessing appropriate treatment.

My professional background includes experience in residential treatment environments, where I developed an appreciation for trauma-informed care, compassionate communication, and the importance of establishing trust with vulnerable populations. My academic studies continue to strengthen my understanding of substance use disorders, behavioral health, and individualized, person-centered approaches to care.

Additionally, through my work as a virtual Spanish language instructor, I independently coordinate online learning sessions, develop individualized educational materials, communicate with families, and facilitate engaging instruction in a remote environment. This experience has strengthened my organizational abilities, technological adaptability, time management, and capacity to establish meaningful professional relationships through virtual communication. My instructional philosophy emphasizes connection before correction, recognizing that effective communication begins with empathy, patience, and an understanding of individual needs.

I am also pursuing education in medical billing and coding, further expanding my understanding of healthcare administration, medical terminology, insurance processes, and accurate, confidential documentation. Together, these educational and professional experiences have equipped me with a multidisciplinary perspective that I believe would translate effectively into behavioral health admissions coordination.

On a personal level, navigating a complex healthcare journey as the parent of a medically complex child has strengthened my advocacy skills, resilience, and ability to communicate with multidisciplinary healthcare teams. This experience has deepened my understanding of the uncertainty families may experience when seeking specialized care and reinforced my commitment to ensuring individuals feel heard, respected, and supported throughout the process.

I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to serve as an initial point of contact for adolescents, adults, and families seeking behavioral health treatment. I recognize the importance of approaching these conversations with professionalism, cultural sensitivity, discretion, and compassion. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my bilingual communication skills, remote instructional experience, educational foundation, and commitment to behavioral healthcare to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to further discuss how my qualifications and dedication to service align with your organization’s mission.

Sincerely,
Allisson Harris

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

RE: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor of Science in Human and Community Advocacy from the University of Texas at San Antonio, an Associate of Arts in Psychology, and professional experience in healthcare, customer service, and public assistance, I bring a combination of professional qualifications, compassion, and a genuine commitment to helping adolescents and families access mental health services.

Throughout my career, including my work with Texas Health and Human Services, healthcare-related call centers, and my current position with Aflac, I have developed strong skills in communication, active listening, documentation, problem-solving, and assisting individuals through complex and sometimes emotionally challenging situations. My experience has taught me the importance of maintaining confidentiality, gathering accurate information, explaining processes clearly, and ensuring that individuals feel respected and supported.

What makes this opportunity particularly meaningful to me is my personal experience as a mother who has navigated the mental health system while advocating for a child experiencing significant emotional and behavioral health challenges. I understand firsthand the fear, uncertainty, and emotional exhaustion that families can experience when trying to find appropriate treatment. My family has navigated hospitalizations, mental health crises, and community-based behavioral health services, including the YES Waiver program. Through those experiences, I witnessed how compassionate professionals can make an extraordinary difference in the lives of both adolescents and their families.

Those experiences strengthened my desire to pursue a career in mental health advocacy. They also taught me the importance of listening without judgment, communicating with empathy, and helping families feel supported during some of their most vulnerable moments. I recognize that an admissions coordinator may be one of the first people a struggling adolescent or concerned parent speaks with, and I would approach that responsibility with professionalism, patience, compassion, and respect.

I am particularly interested in the opportunity to assist families throughout the admissions process, coordinate necessary information, communicate with treatment teams, and help individuals better understand their options for care. My background in telephone-based customer service, healthcare documentation, insurance-related inquiries, and administrative support would allow me to contribute meaningfully while continuing to develop my knowledge of adolescent mental health and substance use treatment.

As I pursue my long-term goal of earning a Master of Social Work, I am seeking an opportunity where my professional skills and personal passion can come together to make a meaningful difference. I would be honored to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s work supporting adolescents and helping families find hope, guidance, and access to appropriate treatment.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my education, experience, and dedication to mental health advocacy would make me a valuable addition to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Jermiane Rodriguez

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Program Director, Virtual IOP position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. Your commitment to providing family-centered, evidence-based mental health services to adolescents aligns closely with my passion for expanding access to high-quality behavioral healthcare and supporting positive outcomes for youth and their families. The opportunity to lead a virtual program while driving growth, quality, and operational excellence is especially appealing given my background in behavioral health leadership and program development.

Throughout my career, I have held progressive leadership positions overseeing clinical and operational performance across outpatient, community-based, and behavioral health programs. Currently serving as a Clinical Director, I lead multidisciplinary teams, manage program operations, monitor performance metrics, ensure regulatory compliance, and drive organizational initiatives designed to improve patient access, quality outcomes, and staff engagement. My experience includes oversight of multiple sites, implementation of standardized processes, management of key performance indicators, staff recruitment and development, and collaboration with executive leadership to support strategic growth initiatives.

What particularly draws me to this role is the opportunity to combine clinical operations with business development and community outreach. Throughout my leadership experience, I have successfully built relationships with referral partners, improved service utilization, optimized workflows, and created systems that support both sustainable growth and exceptional patient care. I understand the importance of census management, admissions conversion, quality assurance, and maintaining compliance within highly regulated healthcare environments.

In addition to my operational expertise, I am passionate about building strong teams and fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. I have extensive experience coaching clinical and administrative staff, creating performance improvement initiatives, and implementing data-driven strategies that enhance both employee engagement and patient satisfaction. My leadership approach is grounded in transparency, servant leadership, and a commitment to achieving measurable outcomes.

I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy's continued growth and to help expand access to innovative virtual behavioral health services for adolescents and families across Florida. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience in behavioral health operations, program leadership, and organizational growth can support your mission and goals.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to speaking with you.

Sincerely,

Christen Estep, RMHCI

RE: Program Director, Virtual Intensive Outpatient Program

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Program Director, Virtual Intensive Outpatient Program position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over 20 years of experience in behavioral health, residential services, and program operations, I bring a strong background in leadership, staff development, clinical coordination, and quality improvement. I am excited about the opportunity to contribute my experience to a growing program focused on improving access to mental health services for adolescents and their families.

Throughout my career, I have held progressively responsible positions, including Behavioral Health Program Manager and Coordinator, overseeing daily operations across multiple outpatient services. In these roles, I supervised more than 21 employees, coordinated multidisciplinary teams, monitored program productivity and spending, and supported operational improvements to strengthen service delivery. My experience also includes admissions coordination, community referrals, staff scheduling, documentation oversight, and maintaining compliance with Medicaid, DCF, CARF, and HIPAA requirements.

My professional background has allowed me to develop a strong understanding of the importance of balancing clinical quality with operational efficiency. I recognize that building a successful program requires more than providing services. It involves developing strong referral relationships, supporting staff, monitoring performance, identifying opportunities for growth, and ensuring that individuals and families receive timely, coordinated care.

Although much of my recent clinical and operational experience has focused on adults with mental health and co-occurring substance use disorders, my earlier experience providing behavioral support services has strengthened my understanding of individualized care, family collaboration, and the importance of early intervention. I believe these experiences provide a valuable foundation for supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy's family-centered approach to adolescent treatment.

I have completed all requirements for my Master of Social Work degree through Walden University and am awaiting official degree conferral. I also hold the Certified Behavioral Health Case Manager Supervisor (CBHCMS) credential and have submitted my application for Florida Registered Clinical Social Work Intern registration. These professional milestones reflect my continued commitment to clinical development, ethical practice, and effective behavioral health leadership.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my leadership experience, operational knowledge, and commitment to quality care to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am particularly interested in contributing to the continued development of its Virtual IOP through strong team leadership, community partnerships, and a consistent focus on program performance and client outcomes.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and professional goals align with the needs of your organization.

Sincerely,

Michelle Antonia Rivera
CBHCMS
MSW Program Completed

To whom it may concern,
My name is Selena, and I am excited to be applying for the primary therapist position at North Carolina's first-ever AWA location! I am an LCSWA with multiple years of experience providing therapeutic support in numerous capacities, including as a behavioral health technician, case manager, and psychotherapist. I've also gained experience in a diverse range of therapeutic settings, such as an inpatient adolescent hospital, PHP/IOP mental health clinics, community health (including in-home), and outpatient therapy. The most influential experiences I've gained have been working in adolescent inpatient and PHP/IOP clinics, in which I became comfortable leading group therapy sessions, providing 1:1 individual therapy as well as family-based therapy, and working collaboratively with clinical teams consisting of numerous disciplines and treatment goals. I've also become comfortable with higher levels of care, which I am able to use to offer clients validation and unconditional positive regard, as these experiences can be exhausting. In my current outpatient work, I primarily work with pre-teens and adolescents, as I witnessed a gap in care for these age groups despite the intensity of these transformative years. I aspire to be a supportive resource to these clients in whatever capacity I am able to, as it is already difficult to be a teen, let alone one who feels misunderstood and alone in the journey.

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA)
Mooresville, NC

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position with Adolescent Wellness Academy in Mooresville, North Carolina. As a Licensed Clinical Social Worker Associate (LCSWA) with a Master of Social Work degree and three years of experience supporting children, adolescents, and families, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to AWA's mission of providing compassionate, evidence-based mental health services to adolescents. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to join the founding clinical team and help establish a supportive, collaborative, and client-centered therapeutic environment.

Throughout my professional experience, I have developed a strong foundation in family-centered treatment, crisis intervention, case management, treatment planning, and trauma-informed care. In my current role as a Family Centered Treatment Specialist with Pinnacle Family Services, I provide individualized treatment and case management services to children and families in home and community settings. I develop treatment plans, facilitate interventions, collaborate with community partners, and support families in navigating challenges while promoting stability, resilience, and improved outcomes. This experience has strengthened my ability to build therapeutic relationships, identify individual and family needs, and implement interventions that support meaningful behavioral and emotional change.

Previously, as a Family Advocate at Pat's Place Child Advocacy Center, I supported children and families navigating difficult and often traumatic circumstances. I provided emotional support, crisis intervention, resource coordination, and advocacy while collaborating with multidisciplinary professionals to prioritize child safety and family well-being. My school social work experience at Hawthorne Academy further strengthened my ability to recognize and address the emotional, behavioral, academic, and social needs of at-risk students while developing interventions and connecting families with appropriate resources.

I believe my background in child and family services provides a valuable foundation for working with adolescents experiencing anxiety, depression, trauma, behavioral challenges, and other mental health concerns. I am passionate about creating a therapeutic space where adolescents feel safe, understood, and empowered to develop healthy coping strategies and recognize their strengths. I also understand the importance of family involvement, interdisciplinary collaboration, individualized treatment planning, and consistent communication in supporting successful clinical outcomes.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical experience, dedication to family-centered care, and passion for adolescent mental health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Being part of a new program would allow me to contribute not only to the care of adolescents and their families but also to the development of a positive clinical culture built on compassion, collaboration, and excellence.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications, experience, and commitment to serving children and families would make me a valuable addition to AWA's founding clinical team.

Sincerely,

Abigail Cornele, MSW, LCSWA

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy
Mooresville, North Carolina

Re: Operations Manager, Behavioral Health

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Operations Manager position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. What particularly attracted me to this opportunity is the chance to be part of a founding team and help establish a supportive, well-organized environment for adolescents and their families. With a Master’s degree in Counselling Psychology, two years of full-time experience working directly with mental health clients, and a background in operations management, staff supervision, and business administration, I believe I can bring a valuable combination of clinical understanding and operational leadership to your new North Carolina location.

As the founder of HAP TherapyCare, I independently established and managed a virtual psychotherapy practice while providing direct mental health services. Beyond working with clients, I was responsible for nearly every aspect of running the practice, including client inquiries, intake, scheduling, billing, clinical documentation, professional referrals, and maintaining appropriate standards of confidentiality and care. This experience gave me an appreciation for how much the quality of a client’s experience depends on what happens behind the scenes. Clear communication, reliable processes, timely follow-up, and a welcoming environment can make a meaningful difference for individuals and families seeking support.

My operational leadership experience extends beyond healthcare. At Toronto Inspection Ltd., I coordinated 10 to 15 field technicians and more than 20 daily site visits across multiple active projects while guiding administrative staff, resolving escalations, and improving documentation processes. I regularly investigated complex operational and billing discrepancies, worked with different stakeholders to identify solutions, and introduced practical improvements to make daily operations more organized and efficient. I also bring experience in employee recruitment, interviewing, onboarding, training, and supervision, along with additional business administration and payroll responsibilities through my work with Saphgen.

One quality I would particularly bring to Adolescent Wellness Academy is a strong sense of ownership. When something is not working, I naturally want to understand why, explore possible solutions, and follow through until the issue is addressed. I enjoy creating structure, supporting colleagues, and finding ways to make people’s work easier without losing sight of the individuals we serve. My counselling background has also shaped how I lead and communicate, with empathy, patience, accountability, and respect for different perspectives.

I understand that launching a new behavioral health clinic requires flexibility, collaboration, and attention to both operational details and the experiences of clients, families, and staff. Although I have not previously managed an adolescent PHP or IOP program, I am eager to build on my existing experience, learn the specific requirements of your programs, and contribute to establishing strong operational foundations from the beginning.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in mental health services, practice management, and operational leadership could support Adolescent Wellness Academy’s expansion into North Carolina. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your team.

Sincerely,
Hareesma Amutha Venkatesan

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in the Operations Manager position with Adolescent Wellness Academy as you prepare to open your first North Carolina clinic. What excites me most about this opportunity is the chance to be part of something that can make a genuine difference in the lives of young people and their families. Throughout my career, I have found the most rewarding part of my work is knowing that what I do has a meaningful impact on someone else's life. That is something I experienced firsthand at Shine Support Services, and it is something I hope to continue in my next role.

At Shine Support Services, I helped build the Supportive Employment Program from the ground up. I operated and developed workflows, internal procedures, training materials, participant resources, and documentation standards to help establish the foundation for daily operations. More importantly, I had the opportunity to work directly with individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, support their goals, and build relationships with their families and community partners. I loved being able to see the difference that consistent support and encouragement could make in someone's confidence, independence, and everyday life. I taught a coping skills class that incorporated Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) practices, giving participants the opportunity to learn and practice healthy coping strategies. Those experiences reminded me that meaningful progress is not always one big milestone. Sometimes it is the smaller moments of growth that make the work so worthwhile.

I also bring leadership and operational experience from Graphic Components, where I led the photopolymer department before being promoted to Project Manager. I coordinated departmental workflow, monitored quality, addressed production challenges, developed procedures and training documentation, and cross-trained employees and prospective hires. This experience strengthened my ability to organize competing priorities, support a team, solve problems, and create systems that help people do their jobs effectively.

My experience working with young people also extends to YPATC, a youth performing arts program in Florida, where my responsibilities ranged from scheduling appointments to teaching theater to children. I enjoyed being part of an environment where I could contribute both behind the scenes and directly to the experiences of young people. I have pursued the 40-hour Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) training coursework, further developing my understanding of behavioral support and different learning and support needs.

What draws me to AWA is the opportunity to bring these experiences together in a setting where the work has such an important purpose. I understand that a successful program depends on more than the services being offered. It also takes thoughtful organization, dependable staff, clear communication, consistent routines, and an environment where young people and their families feel supported. I would be excited to help build that foundation for AWA's North Carolina clinic.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, leadership, and passion for meaningful work could contribute to AWA's founding North Carolina team.

Sincerely,

Erica R. Warriner

November 20, 2026
Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy
Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator
Dear Hiring Team,
When a parent reaches out about their teen's mental health or substance use, that first call matters. They are often scared, tired and unsure where to start. I want to be the calm and caring voice that helps them take the next step. That is why I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role at Adolescent Wellness Academy.
I currently work as a Qualified Mental Health Professional (QMHP) with Exceptional Wellness Inc, where all of my work is done through telehealth. I reach out to parents, schedule first sessions and support clients through skills training, case management and crisis intervention. I am also certified in the CANS and ANSA assessments, so I am used to asking careful questions, gathering the right information and understanding what a family truly needs. Working remotely has taught me to manage my own caseload, stay organized and keep clear documentation on time.
Before this role, I worked for almost two years as a Registered Behavior Technician with children at BlueSprig Pediatrics and Twinkle Autism Therapy. Talking with parents was a big part of that work. I learned how to listen first, stay steady when emotions run high and explain next steps in a way families can follow. I also learned how much follow through matters. When I tell a family I will call them back, I do.
I hold a Bachelor's degree in Psychology from the University of Houston Clear Lake, and I am currently earning my Master's in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at Our Lady of the Lake University. My graduate training helps me understand the concerns that bring families to treatment and the importance of getting teens the right level of care. I also grew up crossing the border between Mexico and the United States every day for school, and I speak English and Spanish fluently. This helps me connect with families from many different backgrounds.
I learn new systems quickly, and I would bring the same organization I use with my clients to tracking inquiries, following up with families and supporting enrollments in your CRM. I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can help families at Adolescent Wellness Academy from their very first call. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Aranza Hernandez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I'm excited to apply for the Creative Group Facilitator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a background in Studio Art and Psychology, as well as experience in Special Education and Applied Behavior Analysis, I have always been drawn to the ways creativity can help us connect, express ourselves, and discover more about who we are. I would love the opportunity to bring this perspective into a setting that supports adolescents through their mental health journeys.

In my current role as a SpEd Art Teacher, I work with students with diverse learning needs, developing creative activities to encourage their exploration and independence. My approach to art is centered on the process rather than the final product; I believe the arts should be an opportunity to experiment, take risks, make mistakes, and express yourself without the pressure of getting something "right." My previous experience as an ABA Teacher has also taught me the importance of meeting individuals where they are and creating supportive environments where everyone feels welcome to participate.

My creative background extends beyond visual art to include writing, music, and theatre. These experiences have deepened my appreciation for the many ways people communicate and express themselves, and I'm drawn to opportunities that allow others to explore those possibilities.

My connection to art is also personal. Throughout my own experiences, creativity has been a meaningful way to process and make sense of my emotions. I've come to appreciate the value of having the space to process without judgement or expectations. This is an environment I hope to foster for others; one where individuals feel safe to explore their emotions, connect with each other, and perhaps even learn something new about themselves along the way.

I would be grateful for the chance to contribute my creativity and enthusiasm for the therapeutic arts to the AWA community. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Best,
Charity Ortiz, BA, RBT

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I’m applying for the Social Media Manager position because I enjoy turning real moments into content that helps people feel connected. I’d love to bring that approach to AWA by capturing community events, highlighting your team, and helping teens and their families learn what support can look like.

Through my work with Allure Her, I’ve helped plan social media content, write captions, and edit short-form videos that reflect the brand’s voice. I’ve also edited content for 450 Pro Services and supported livestreams as part of my church’s media team. Those experiences have taught me how to capture moments as they happen and shape them into stories that work across different platforms.

At AWA, I’d bring that same care to everything from short event recaps to LinkedIn posts that show what it’s like to work with your team. I understand that sharing stories in a behavioral health setting comes with a responsibility to protect client privacy. I’d follow AWA’s consent and approval procedures, protect identifying details, and use language that treats teens and families with dignity.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to share my portfolio and discuss how I could help tell AWA’s story.

Best,
Shelby Risque

Sincerely,

 Anna Babinchak

candidates.cover_letter:
Soy Thelma Castillo soy Nicaraguense, psicóloga de profesión, de vocación me gusta ayudar a las poblaciones vulnerables, además de dar capacitaciones en diferentes temas de interés y necesidad para diferentes grupos de personas en edades, etnias y cultura. En mi trayectoria profesional es enriquecedor, dar y aprender de cada una de las personas que me rodean. 

Tengo aproximadamente 25 años de experiencia en diversas áreas de la psicología, inicie en la psicología social,  de voluntaria en la Red Nacional contra la Violencia Doméstica, al finalizar la universidad trabajé un tiempo con adolescentes en riesgo de violencia y explotación sexual y en los último 23 años fui consejera escolar en los niveles desde preescolar, primaria y secundaria en colegios privados de Managua, Nicaragua, apoyando los procesos psicoeducativos de los estudiantes, brindando asesoría a los docentes y dando consejería individual y grupal a los padres de familia.

Actualmente resido en Miami desde el 2023, y tengo 3 años de trabajar con personas de la tercera edad. 

Gracias por su atención a esta breve presentación.

Saludos

Thelma Castillo.
